springwarm.summary: You glow in warm, yellow-based colors with enough saturation to look fresh and sunny.
overview: True Spring is the warmest of the three spring types. A golden undertone runs through your skin, hair, and eyes, which gives you a sunlit, lively look. It is also a fairly uncommon type, so many people with this coloring spend years unsure which shades truly suit them.

The key words for you are yellow warmth and real saturation. Rather than very pale pastels, you look best in colors a step richer: apricot orange, warm spring green, or an egg-yolk yellow. Cool, blue-toned or grayed-out shades tend to drain your complexion and make you look tired.

A reliable approach is to build outfits on warm neutrals such as beige, camel, and brown, then add one or two cheerful accents in orange, yellow, or green. Mixing a couple of warm colors playfully brings out the lovely energy that defines this type.
features: Skin: Clear skin with a yellow or peachy undertone. It tends to tan golden rather than turn red, and a soft apricot flush often shows on the cheeks.
Hair: Warm light-to-medium brown or honey-brown rather than deep black, often with golden or coppery highlights in sunlight.
Eyes: Light brown, amber, or golden brown eyes that look clear and warm and sparkle against the whites.
Overall impression: Bright, friendly, and playful. Your complexion looks lively, you can come across as youthful, and a smile carries a lot of warmth.
bestColors: Apricot, coral pink, and peach: warm pinks and oranges with a yellow base that add healthy color to your face.
Egg-yolk yellow, warm mustard-leaning yellow, and golden tones flatter a clear complexion.
Fresh lime, warm leaf green, and vivid blue-leaning green give a crisp, refreshing feel.
Warm neutrals such as camel, light brown, and cream beige make a dependable base, and terracotta-style reddish browns work well too.
avoidColors: Stark optical white or icy, blue-based shades can make your skin look pale and cold.
Blue-toned pinks, royal blue, and sky blue clash with your yellow undertone and make your face look washed out.
Dusty, grayed-out colors, heavy dark neutrals worn alone, and low-contrast monochrome outfits all dull your natural glow.
makeup: Base: Choose a beige with a yellow or apricot lean and avoid shades that sit too white. A light, dewy finish adds life.
Eyes: Gold brown, orange brown, and warm copper shadows brighten the eye area. Dark brown liner looks softer than harsh black.
Blush: Peach, apricot, or soft orange-coral on the apples of the cheeks gives a playful flush.
Lips: Clear, saturated coral, orange red, and warm apricot pink work best. Blue-leaning pinks and purple tones can darken your face.
fashion: Start with beige, camel, or brown and lift it with a vivid orange, yellow, or green top or scarf. Warm neutrals plus a bright accent is your most flattering formula.
Choose cream or ivory instead of pure white for a softer look near the face. For denim, a clear mid-tone blue is easier to wear than an icy one.
Cotton, linen, and light knits suit your cheerful energy. Playful checks or large prints usually flatter you more than tiny, fussy patterns.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Light brown, golden brown, and warm caramel shades suit you. Blue-black or ash tones can look disconnected from your skin.
Accessories: Shiny gold is your best metal. Delicate chains and small pendants keep things light, and if you wear silver, avoid very cold, mirror-like finishes.
Glasses and small items: Gold, honey brown, or tortoiseshell frames feel warm and natural. Bags and shoes in camel or cognac leather tie an outfit together.
springwarm.compare: True Spring shares a season with Bright Spring and Light Spring, but each has a different center. Bright Spring relies on strong contrast and very vivid color, while True Spring is led by yellow warmth, so beige and brown bases with bright accents suit you better. Light Spring shines in pale, softened colors, whereas True Spring can handle deeper, more saturated ones. True Autumn also shares your warmth, but it is richer and calmer, while you are brighter and clearer. At the far end, True Winter's cold, blue-based colors are the least flattering for you.

springbright.summary: Clear, saturated colors and sharp contrast make you shine at your most vivid.
overview: Bright Spring combines the warm, sunny energy of spring with the crisp contrast of winter. The difference between your skin, hair, and eyes is noticeable, which makes your features look defined and gives you an eye-catching, vivid presence.

Your color range is wide. You can wear light and dark, warm and even cool shades, with one condition: the color must be clear. Fresh, fruity brights suit you, while smoky, grayed-out shades quickly make your face look tired.

Contrast matters as much as saturation. Pairing white with black, or bright yellow with deep navy, makes your face look sharper and livelier. Bold combinations work far better for you than soft, matching tones layered together.
features: Skin: Clear, bright, and fairly translucent, with a slight yellow or peach undertone and a lively flush that looks healthy and clean.
Hair: Often deep brown to dark brown-black with a healthy shine, which creates strong contrast with your skin.
Eyes: Distinct dark or deep brown eyes that sparkle. The clear contrast with the whites gives your gaze a bright, strong feel.
Overall impression: Energetic, colorful, and sharp. The contrast between skin, hair, and eyes keeps your face from looking faded in photos.
bestColors: Clear coral red, tomato red, and orange red: bright, warm reds and oranges that light up your face.
Lemon yellow, bright golden yellow, and lime green give a zesty, energetic look.
Turquoise, clear teal, and vivid blue also work well. Mixing them with warm colors sharpens the contrast.
Vivid violet and magenta pink are good accents, and cream white paired with deep brown or charcoal gives useful light-dark contrast.
avoidColors: Smoky, grayed-out shades such as muddy greige or dusty lavender dull your complexion.
A single washed-out pastel worn alone weakens your look. Use it only as a small accent next to clear colors.
Tone-on-tone outfits in similar lightness and saturation remove the contrast that is your strength and can look flat.
makeup: Base: Go for a bright, clear beige with a translucent finish. A thin, slightly dewy glow supports your clean look more than a heavy matte one.
Eyes: Start with a brown base and add a vivid accent such as clear coral, gold, or teal on the outer corner or liner to sharpen your gaze.
Blush: Bright coral or warm pink applied high on the cheeks gives a lively flush. Skip muddy mauve shades.
Lips: Clear coral red, orange red, or cherry with strong color payoff completes the contrast in your face.
fashion: Pair two colors that differ strongly, such as white with black or navy with yellow. Clear light-dark contrast within one outfit makes your face stand out.
Wear bold red, turquoise, or yellow tops and dresses without worry. Choosing a single accent color is enough to keep the look tidy.
Smooth, crisp fabrics like clean cotton or glossy satin match your sharp look. Very slouchy textures or tiny, busy prints can blur your impact.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Glossy deep brown or dark chocolate keeps your contrast strong. If you color it, choose a clear brown without blue tones and avoid dull ash shades.
Accessories: Shiny gold is your best match, and bright gemstones or enamel accents also work. Pieces with some presence balance your striking features.
Glasses and small items: Crisp black, dark brown, or bold colored frames suit you. Adding one vivid bag or scarf makes the whole outfit feel lively.
springbright.compare: Bright Spring looks similar to True Spring and Light Spring but is centered differently. True Spring is led by yellow warmth, so beige and brown bases suit it, while you can also wear some cool shades and rely on strong contrast and clarity. Light Spring glows in pale, softened colors, but you look best in much more vivid ones. Bright Winter, your neighbor type, shares your clarity and contrast, though you lean toward warm, yellow-based colors and Bright Winter leans toward cold, blue-based ones.

springlight.summary: Light, softly warm colors with a touch of white bring out your clear, fresh look.
overview: Light Spring wears the fresh colors of early spring most naturally. Your complexion looks clear and light, and your overall feel is soft and gentle. Bright shades that remind you of ice cream or new petals wrap your face in a glow.

Like True Spring, you can wear many colors, but you are most comfortable in lighter, less saturated versions with a bit of white in them. Cream, ivory, pale apricot, spring green, and soft yellow are safe choices, and a few soft cool tones can be mixed in.

Very dark or heavy colors tend to be noticed before your face is. Pure black and cold, pale shades in particular can overpower your light feel. When you need something deeper, choose a softer option such as soft brown or a warm navy.
features: Skin: Light, delicate-looking skin, often with a faint yellow or peach undertone and a gentle pink or apricot flush on the cheeks.
Hair: Soft brown or light chestnut rather than deep black, sometimes with a pale golden shine in the sun.
Eyes: Light brown or pale amber eyes that look clear and transparent. The gaze feels soft rather than intense.
Overall impression: Bright, light, and kind. With low contrast between features, you often look youthful and sweet.
bestColors: Cream, ivory, and pale butter yellow are warm, soft light colors that make a great base.
Pale apricot, peach, and light coral pink: warm pinks and oranges with white mixed in brighten your face.
Sprout green, mint, and pale turquoise bring a fresh and airy mood.
Soft sky blue, lavender, and light purple make good accents, and sand beige or light camel serve as calm basics.
avoidColors: Pure black or very deep charcoal feels heavy and can overpower your light impression.
Strongly blue-based vivid colors such as deep magenta, dark purple, and intense royal blue clash with your soft mood.
Cold, chalky pastels and grayed-out dusty colors can make your skin look dry and tired.
makeup: Base: Apply a light, translucent beige or pale apricot base thinly. A sheer finish keeps your fresh look better than heavy coverage.
Eyes: Pale peach, champagne gold, and soft camel brown suit you. Keep liner thin and use soft brown instead of deep black.
Blush: Diffuse light peach or apricot pink gently over the cheeks. Build stronger colors slowly in thin layers.
Lips: Light coral, peach pink, and clear apricot that go on sheer look best, and a glossy finish adds sweetness.
fashion: Tone-on-tone looks in light, soft colors suit you, such as pale apricot over cream or ivory with spring green.
When you need a dark piece, pick soft brown or gentle navy over true black, and keep a light top near the face for balance.
Thin knits, chiffon, and light cotton in soft textures work well. Tiny floral prints or gentle checks add to your fresh charm.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Light brown, milk-tea brown, and soft caramel suit you. Very dark black can create too much contrast and feel heavy.
Accessories: Pale gold and rose gold with a gentle shine are good, as are small pearls or clear stones. Very large, thick pieces may feel overwhelming.
Glasses and small items: Clear, pale beige, or light gold frames protect your soft look. Bags and shoes in ivory or light camel blend well with the rest.
springlight.compare: Among the spring types, Light Spring is the lightest and softest. True Spring relies on yellow warmth and deeper saturation, so it carries rich colors like orange or mustard, while you look better in paler versions of the same hues. Bright Spring thrives on sharp contrast and vivid color, but you do better with less contrast and gentler blending. Light Summer, your neighbor type, shares your light, airy feel, but you lean toward warm, yellow-based colors whereas Light Summer leans toward cool, blue-based ones.

summercool.summary: A fresh, elegant cool-toned type that glows in clear blues, rosy pinks, and soft lavenders.
overview: True Summer is the coolest and cleanest-looking of the summer types. Your skin tends to carry a hint of blue or rosy pink, so colors with a drop of blue or violet in them make your face look bright and awake, while yellow-based shades can feel flat. It is one of the more common types in Korea, so you may spot it often around you.

The key idea is medium saturation with a clearly cool temperature. Instead of loud primary colors, think of colors that have been diluted with a little cool water: a clear sky blue, lavender, or a rosy pink. Warm shades like mustard or orange near the face can make skin look sallow or tired.
Value contrast works well for you. Pairing navy with light blue, or charcoal with white, keeps everything inside the cool family while creating a neat, polished look.
features: Skin: Often fair with a blue or pink undertone. In the sun you tend to flush pink rather than tan golden, and veins may look bluish.
Hair: Soft dark brown or ash-leaning black suits you, and natural hair color usually reads calm and without much red.
Eyes: Deep brown or gray-brown, with a soft edge between the iris and the white rather than a sharp, dramatic line.
Overall impression: Clean, graceful, and composed. People tend to remember a cool, clear atmosphere rather than a bold one.
bestColors: Blues: clear sky blue, a fresh cobalt-leaning blue, and deep navy, anything with a definite blue base.
Pinks and roses: rosy pink, soft magenta, and berry tones rather than peachy ones give your cheeks a natural lift.
Lavenders and purples: from pale lavender through orchid to deep plum and violet, you can wear nearly the whole range.
Grays and cool greens: cool gray, charcoal, and icy greens such as minty teal or emerald look crisp and clean.
avoidColors: Yellows and mustards: strong yellow or muddy mustard can make your face look sallow and tired.
Oranges and terracotta: orange and brick shades clash with your blue undertone and can feel disconnected from your face.
Khaki, olive, and golden browns: dark yellow-based greens and browns tend to dull your complexion.
makeup: Base: Choose a pink beige or cool beige with little yellow, and aim for a clear, fresh glow instead of heavy coverage.
Eyes: Rose brown, cool taupe, soft lilac, and gray-brown shadows suit you. Keep shimmer silvery or pink.
Blush: A blue-toned rose pink or a lavender-leaning pink applied softly across the cheeks brings out a clear flush.
Lips: Rose pink, berry, and fresh bluish pinks look lovely. For a deeper lip, choose wine or raspberry for a refined finish.
fashion: Put cool shades near your face: a sky blue shirt, a lavender knit, or a rosy blouse can make your skin look brighter.
Neat contrast combinations like a navy blazer over white or charcoal trousers with a pale blue shirt look especially polished.
Smooth, crisp fabrics like cotton, linen, and fine knits suit you. If you usually reach for beige or camel, try cool gray or navy instead.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Ash brown, dark chocolate, and calm black-brown work well. Soft cool browns usually flatter more than red or golden dyes.
Accessories: Silver, white gold, and platinum look best, and pearls or pale blue stones add a graceful touch.
Glasses and extras: Thin silver, clear, navy, or cool gray frames look tidy. Add pops of navy, lavender, or rose pink with scarves and bags.
summercool.compare: True Summer shares its cool undertone with True Winter, but True Winter handles sharp, high-contrast colors while True Summer shines in colors that are a little softer. Compared with Light Summer, who leans toward lighter and airier pastels, you can wear cool colors with more depth and saturation. Compared with Soft Summer, who looks best in gray-tinged hazy shades, you suit clearer, cleaner colors. If you are unsure, hold a clear rosy pink and a dusty pink up to your face in turn, and notice which one makes your skin look more transparent.

summermute.summary: A gentle, dreamy type that looks best in soft, low-saturation colors like a misty dawn.
overview: Soft Summer feels like a hazy, cool summer just before autumn arrives. Your skin, eyes, and hair blend together softly, so strong colors can overpower you and make the color stand out more than your face. When a color has a touch of gray in it, you and your clothes look like one calm, harmonious picture.

Think of muted as turned down in saturation. A dusty rose suits you better than a bright pink, and a smoky blue works better than a vivid one. Cool shades are your base, but softly warm, muted colors can work too, so your range is wider than you might expect.
The main principle is gentle contrast. Instead of pure white against black, layer closer shades like ivory, grayish beige, and dark gray for a quiet, refined look.
features: Skin: A softly settled tone mixing blue and yellow undertones, often with a matte, gentle finish. Redness usually isn't very pronounced.
Hair: Soft dark brown or ash-toned brown, with a diffuse sheen rather than sparkling highlights in the sun.
Eyes: Light brown or gray-brown with a soft look, and the edge of the eye tends to blend smoothly instead of being sharply defined.
Overall impression: Dreamy, gentle, and quiet. The first impression is not loud, but it feels more comfortable and charming the longer people look.
bestColors: Pinks: dusty rose, soft rose pink, and mauve pink, where a touch of gray softens the color.
Blues: smoky blue, slate blue, and pale powder blue that look like fog on the water.
Purples and grays: muted lavender, grayish purple, medium-depth plum, and mid-tone cool gray feel steady and elegant.
Greens and creams: soft mint, sage-like muted green, and pale cream yellow can surprisingly work as well.
avoidColors: Vivid primaries: bright red and neon-like pink or lime show before your face does and can feel overwhelming.
Strong yellow and orange: saturated shades can look disconnected from your skin and make you appear tired.
Extreme light-dark contrast: stark white, jet black, and intense cobalt can make your face look washed out, so choose softer versions.
makeup: Base: Choose a neutral or pale pink beige with neither too much yellow nor pink, and finish with a thin, smooth semi-matte look.
Eyes: Mauve brown, grayish rose, taupe, and soft khaki shadows suit you. Keep shimmer very fine and subtle.
Blush: A dusty rose or pale mauve pink, blended thinly, creates a natural flush.
Lips: Rose beige, dusty pink, and mauve rose in a blurred, softly dabbed finish look beautiful.
fashion: Smoky blue shirts, dusty pink knits, and lavender-gray cardigans keep a gentle, hazy color close to your face.
Choose ivory over white and dark gray or dark brown over black, and keep colors close in value for tone-on-tone outfits.
Soft fabrics like cashmere-feel knits, washed cotton, and light chiffon suit you. Try to wear less shiny material.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Ash brown, soft chocolate, and grayish brown work best. Very bright or strongly yellow dyes can feel disconnected from your skin tone.
Accessories: Rose gold, matte silver, and softly lustrous pearls suit you. Small, delicate pieces beat large, flashy ones.
Glasses and extras: Clear, soft gray, or mauve brown frames feel gentle. Add scarves or bags in hazy dusty blue or lavender.
summermute.compare: Soft Summer shares its soft, hazy quality with Soft Autumn, but Soft Autumn feels at home in warm olive and camel bases while you look better on the cool side with a faint blue undertone. Compared with True Summer, who shines in clear, clean colors, you look more natural in colors that have gray mixed in. Light Summer is airy and bright in pastels, while you have a bit more settled depth. If you are not sure, hold a vivid pink and a dusty pink to your face in turn and choose the one that makes your skin look softer.

summerlight.summary: A clear, airy type that glows in pale sky blue and pink pastel shades.
overview: Light Summer is the clearest and brightest of the summer types. Your skin often looks thin and translucent, so light colors that seem lit by the sun suit you far better than heavy, deep ones. You are a cool base, with a faint hint of Light Spring's warmth and liveliness peeking through.

The most important factor for you is lightness. A clear sky blue brightens your face more than a deep navy, and a gentle lavender flatters you more than a dark plum. The lighter and more transparent the color, the more your natural clarity comes out, as if a thin layer of light is resting on you.
That said, you do not have to avoid dark colors entirely. Place them on trousers or shoes, far from your face, and keep brighter shades near your face to stay balanced.
features: Skin: Often fair with a thin, translucent look and a soft pink glow. It can flush easily in the sun, so sun protection is worth a thought.
Hair: Soft light brown or lighter brown tones with a lightweight feel that looks clear in the sunlight.
Eyes: Light brown or a clear amber shade, giving a bright and kind gaze.
Overall impression: Clean, refreshing, and light. The soft, radiant vibe tends to leave a friendly first impression.
bestColors: Blues: clear sky blue, pale powder blue, and soft periwinkle, bright and transparent shades suit you best.
Pinks: candy pink, light rose, and cherry blossom pink bring a lively glow to your face.
Lavenders and purples: soft lilac, pale lavender, and mid-tone blue violet blend in gently.
Neutrals: cool gray, a light and slightly warm beige, mauve beige, and mint green offer a clean backdrop.
avoidColors: Dark, heavy browns and khakis: deep chocolate, olive, and dark khaki can weigh your face down and make it look dull.
Burgundy and deep wine: dark reds and rich plum hide your natural clarity and may make you look tired.
Mustard, terracotta, and black: muddy yellow, brick tones, and pure black can overpower your soft look.
makeup: Base: Pick a light pink beige or neutral ivory and finish with a thin, dewy layer to keep your skin looking translucent. Skip heavy coverage.
Eyes: Peach pink, soft rose, lavender, and light taupe suit you. Keep shimmer fine and softly sparkling.
Blush: Light pink or soft coral pink dabbed on the center of the cheeks gives a radiant flush.
Lips: Coral pink, rose pink, and sheer strawberry-milk pinks suit you, and a clear glossy texture works nicely.
fashion: A white tee with jeans, a sky blue shirt, or a light pink knit gives a clean, refreshing look.
When layering pastels, group similar-value shades like ivory, lavender, and baby blue for a soft, luminous outfit.
Light fabrics such as thin cotton, airy chiffon, and fluffy knits feel right. Use heavy leather or thick dark material only for trousers or accessories.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Light brown, milk brown, and soft ash beige look lovely. A very dark, intense black can make your face look heavy.
Accessories: White gold, silver, and subtle rose gold work well, and small pearls and clear stones add a fresh touch.
Glasses and extras: Thin clear, pale pink, or soft gray frames are a good fit. Add pastel blue or lilac scarves and bags as accents.
summerlight.compare: Light Summer shares its light, airy feeling with Light Spring, but Light Spring is comfortable in peachy and warm coral shades, while you look more natural in bluish pinks and sky blues. Compared with True Summer, who handles cool colors with more depth and saturation, you suit paler and more transparent pastels. Soft Summer is calm in gray-tinged shades, whereas you look best in clear shades with little gray. If you are unsure, hold a pale sky blue and a smoky blue to your face in turn and pick the one that makes you look brighter.

autumnwarm.summary: The warmest of the autumn types, glowing in golden, earthy colors like maple leaves in late sun.
overview: True Autumn is the autumn type with the strongest yellow and red undertones. Skin, hair, and eyes all tend to carry a golden-brown warmth, so colors with a similar temperature make your face look bright and balanced. Colors with a blue cast, on the other hand, can make your complexion look dull or sallow.

The key to this type is warm color with medium-to-rich saturation. Mustard, olive, brick, terracotta, and orange-red are the classics, all borrowed from soil and fallen leaves. Very pale pastels and very dark inky shades tend to be less flattering than mid-depth colors that look ripened and full.

At first, a wardrobe of browns and golds may feel predictable, but texture makes all the difference. Suede, corduroy, chunky knits, and leather bring out the rich, generous mood that suits True Autumn so well.
features: Skin: Often has a yellow or golden warmth, with veins that tend to look greenish. In the sun it usually tans lightly rather than burning red.
Hair: Deep brown, chestnut, or hair that glints copper in sunlight. Even very dark hair often has a brown cast rather than a blue-black one.
Eyes: Amber, hazel-brown, or deep warm brown, typically with a soft edge around the iris instead of a sharp, crisp outline.
Overall impression: Calm, generous, and elegant. You rarely look flashy, but the longer people spend near you, the more warmth they feel.
bestColors: Mustard and golden yellow: From vivid yellow to amber, golden yellows light up your skin. Keep them close to your face in a knit or scarf for the biggest effect.
Olive and moss green: Yellow-leaning greens such as olive, moss, and khaki are signature True Autumn shades and look natural and refined.
Terracotta, brick, and orange-red: These reddish browns and warm oranges bring healthy color to your face and make great accent pieces.
Camel, chocolate brown, and teal: Camel and deep brown work as dependable basics, while a warm turquoise or deep teal adds a refreshing pop.
avoidColors: Blue-toned pink and lavender: Icy pinks, purples, and pale lilac can emphasize the yellow in your skin and make your complexion look muddy.
Cool gray and stark white: Icy gray or bright optic white tends to float apart from your face. If you need a light neutral, choose ivory or cream.
Vivid cool blues and neon pink: Sky blue, cobalt, and magenta clash with your warmth, so the outfit is noticed before your face.
makeup: Base: Choose a beige with a slight golden undertone so it blends into your skin. Avoid chalky, pale finishes; a natural glow works well.
Eyes: Bronze, khaki, copper, and warm brown shadows add depth. Dark brown liner is much softer on you than black.
Blush: Apricot, coral, and warm orange shades give a healthy flush. Cool pinks can look disconnected from your skin.
Lips: Brick, terracotta, orange-red, and brick-brown are classic. Choose a rich, warm red over a bright fuchsia.
fashion: Fabric and texture: Knits, wool, suede, corduroy, and leather look best. The same color feels richer in a natural texture than in slick synthetic fabric.
Patterns: Large checks, paisley, and bold florals suit you better than tiny prints. Stick to earthy combinations of brown, olive, and mustard.
Outfit formula: A camel coat over an olive knit with brown trousers is a safe tone-on-tone look. One accent in orange or terracotta is all you need.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Chocolate brown, copper brown, and other warm browns suit you. Ash tones or blue-black can separate from your skin.
Accessories: Yellow gold, rose gold, and bronze are the best metals. Natural materials like amber, wood, leather, and tortoiseshell add to the mood.
Glasses and small items: Brown tortoiseshell or gold frames work well, while cool silver or clear blue frames are less flattering. Choose camel or cognac for bags and belts.
autumnwarm.compare: Compared with Soft Autumn, True Autumn is much more vivid and warm. Soft Autumn loves muted, grayed colors, while True Autumn carries yellow and red tones with confidence. Dark Autumn shines in deeper, heavier shades, whereas True Autumn is happiest in golden, mid-depth colors. True Spring shares the warmth but suits clear, bright shades, while True Autumn is better in deeper, calmer ones. Its opposite, True Summer, is the reverse in both temperature and saturation, so the pinkish pastels that flatter True Summer can wash out True Autumn.

autumnmute.summary: A gentle, vintage-minded type that glows in soft, low-saturation colors with a warm, hazy feel.
overview: Soft Autumn has the quiet warmth of a lazy autumn afternoon. The defining feature of this type is softness: colors with a little gray, beige, or milk mixed in blend naturally with your face and create a relaxed, refined impression.

Bright, intense colors tend to be noticed before your face and can make your skin look tired. Sand, oatmeal, khaki, and mocha, which look as if seen through a light mist, soften your features and make everything look in harmony.

Soft Autumn shines in low-contrast outfits. Rather than splitting light and dark sharply, layer colors of similar depth for a luxurious feel. Vintage accessories and soft textures bring out the best in this type.
features: Skin: Often softly warm with a subtle yellow cast. Even with some redness, the overall look is muted and calm, with a natural texture rather than a glossy one.
Hair: Soft brown, dark brown, or gentle golden-brown. Hair is often fine and smooth, with a quiet sheen instead of a strong shine.
Eyes: Light brown, hazel, or brown with an olive hint. The edge between iris and white often looks soft and blended.
Overall impression: Gentle and approachable, with low facial contrast. People often say you seem easy to talk to from the first meeting.
bestColors: Beige, oatmeal, and sand: Milky light browns smooth your complexion. They work especially well in shirts and inner layers near your face.
Khaki, sage, and olive: Grayed greens, from pale moss to deep olive, are signature Soft Autumn colors and create a calm, thoughtful mood.
Mocha, cocoa, and dark brown: A slightly muted brown is an excellent replacement for black. Choose browns with a hint of gray over very saturated ones.
Dusty teal, mustard, and apricot orange: Muted teal, soft yellow, and gentle orange make good accents. Just one is enough to add life.
avoidColors: Neons and vivid colors: Hot pink, neon yellow, and electric blue overpower your face and can make your skin look dull.
Optic white: Stark white can make your skin look yellow. Try cream, ivory, or oatmeal instead.
Cold cobalt and deep icy navy: Cold, blue-heavy shades make your soft look feel stiff. For blue, choose dusty blue or washed denim.
makeup: Base: Pick a medium tone without excess yellow or pink, with a soft matte finish rather than heavy highlighter.
Eyes: Satin sand, taupe, khaki, and mocha brown deepen the eyes gently. Choose fine shimmer over chunky glitter.
Blush: Dusty rose, soft peach, and light terracotta add natural color. Avoid bright pinks.
Lips: Rose beige, mauve brown, nude brick, and dried-rose shades work best. A soft matte texture suits you more than a glossy bright red.
fashion: Fabric and texture: Cotton, linen, soft knits, denim, and lace feel natural and warm. Matte or textured fabrics are better than high-shine ones.
Patterns: Vintage florals, small checks, and gentle stripes with low color contrast suit you. Skip large logos and bold graphics.
Outfit formula: Layer an oatmeal knit with khaki trousers and a mocha bag, keeping the depth similar. Dark brown with cream is far softer than black and white.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Milk-tea brown, hazelnut brown, and soft dark brown suit you. Very light blonde or blue-black can separate from your face.
Accessories: Matte gold, copper, and antique bronze work better than high-shine metals. Pearls, wooden beads, and vintage coins also fit.
Glasses and small items: Half-rim brown frames, thin gold frames, or translucent amber frames keep the look soft. Choose low-shine mocha or camel leather.
autumnmute.compare: Compared with True Autumn, Soft Autumn is lower in saturation and carries a gray softness. True Autumn glows in vivid mustard and orange-red, but Soft Autumn is more comfortable when even yellow and orange are slightly muted. Dark Autumn comes alive in deep, rich colors, while Soft Autumn looks more natural in gentle, low-contrast ones. The type most often confused with it is Soft Summer: both suit muted colors, but Soft Summer leans toward cool, bluish grays while Soft Autumn leans toward warm, yellowish browns. Bright Winter is its opposite in clarity and contrast, so neon shades are especially hard to wear.

autumndeep.summary: A rich, mature type that glows in deep, weighty warm colors with a luxurious, late-autumn mood.
overview: Dark Autumn suits the deepest, darkest colors in the autumn family. Think of late autumn, just before winter, when leaves have turned dark and the sun sets early. The warmth remains, but your features come alive in low-lightness, rich shades.

Burgundy, dark chocolate, deep green, rich olive, and dark navy all suit this type. They sharpen your outline and create a mature, sophisticated impression. Neon or pale pastel shades tend to make the clothes stand out more than your face.

Unlike other autumn types, Dark Autumn can also wear some dark cool colors. Deep burgundy, wine, and deep teal are fine even with a slight blue cast, as long as they are rich enough. Pale or hazy cool tones, however, still do not suit you.
features: Skin: Often medium to deep with a yellow or olive warmth. Even lighter skin can look more calm and deep than glowing.
Hair: Dark brown, black-brown, or near-black, often thick and full-bodied.
Eyes: Deep brown or black-brown, where the iris and pupil blend together. The gaze often feels deep and heavy.
Overall impression: Defined, mature, and charismatic. You have presence even without decorations.
bestColors: Burgundy, wine, and deep red: The dark wine and strong red shades in the palette add natural flush to your face. They work as main colors or accents.
Deep green, olive, and forest: Dark olive and forest green are signature Dark Autumn colors, giving coats and knits a refined, layered look.
Dark chocolate, espresso, and cognac: Deep browns are the most dependable basics and anchor almost any outfit. They also pair well with soft black.
Deep teal, dark petrol, and mustard gold: Rich teal and dark navy add a cool accent, while dark golden shades bring brightness.
avoidColors: Pale pastel blue and baby pink: Light, white-tinted blues and pinks look weak and can make you appear tired.
Hazy gray and lavender: Pale gray and lilac blur the strong definition of your features.
Neon and bright pink: Light, clear neon shades clash with your weighty mood, so the outfit overpowers your face.
makeup: Base: Choose a medium beige with a healthy glow and avoid very light shades that float on your skin. Contouring suits you well.
Eyes: Dark brown, copper, bronze, and deep olive shadows enhance deep-set eyes. Smoky makeup is easy for you to carry off.
Blush: Terracotta, deep coral, and brick shades work best. Apply a slightly muted tone rather than a bright pink.
Lips: Wine, burgundy, brick red, and dark chocolate brown suit you. A matte or velvet finish adds sophistication.
fashion: Fabric and texture: Wool coats, cashmere knits, velvet, leather, and suede suit you. Substantial fabrics add stability to your overall look.
Patterns: Large checks, paisley, exotic florals, and animal prints in deep colors work well. Avoid delicate pastel prints.
Outfit formula: Layer deep shades, like a dark brown coat with a burgundy knit and a deep green scarf. When using black, choose charcoal or soft black over harsh jet black.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Dark chocolate, red-wine brown, and soft black-brown suit you. Very light dyes can hide the depth in your face.
Accessories: Rich metals like gold, antique gold, and bronze work, especially in bold, statement designs. Deep gemstones like garnet, amber, and obsidian match your mood.
Glasses and small items: Thick brown or tortoiseshell frames and gold metal frames add an intelligent, solid look. Choose espresso or wine leather for bags and shoes.
autumndeep.compare: Compared with True Autumn, Dark Autumn shines in darker, heavier shades. True Autumn is most comfortable in golden, mid-depth colors, while Dark Autumn does better in a deeper version of the same shades. Unlike Soft Autumn, Dark Autumn suits rich, clear colors more than soft, grayed ones. Dark Winter is the nearest relative: both suit dark colors, but Dark Winter prefers cool, blue-leaning contrast while Dark Autumn is more natural in warm browns and reddish shades. Its opposite, Light Summer, is reversed in both lightness and softness, so pale pastels are especially tricky for Dark Autumn.

wintercool.summary: Cool, crisp, high-contrast colors bring out your clear, sharp features.
overview: True Winter is the coolest of the winter types. When you wear clear, icy colors with no yellow in them, your skin looks translucent and the contrast between your eyes, hair and complexion becomes striking.

Two ideas matter most: coolness and contrast. The color itself should lean blue, and the outfit should pair light with dark, such as white with black, or sapphire with hot pink. Strongly separated combinations suit you best.
Warm, yellow-leaning shades and softly faded colors can make your face look tired or sallow. When choosing clothes, check the undertone first, then the clarity, then the light-dark gap.
features: Skin: Often fair with a blue or pink undertone rather than a yellow one, with a clear, calm look. Some people flush easily in the sun.
Hair: Typically glossy dark brown or blue-leaning black. The depth of the hair creates a clear contrast with the skin.
Eyes: Usually deep brown to near black, with a crisp edge between iris and white that gives a strong gaze.
Overall impression: Cool, polished and urban. Your features read clearly, so you have presence even when you are quiet.
bestColors: Pure white and cool gray: optic white, silvery gray and charcoal make a clean foundation.
Jewel blues and teals: sapphire, cobalt, clear sky blue and emerald green brighten your complexion.
Blue-based pinks and purples: magenta, fuchsia and deep orchid are signature colors for True Winter.
Ruby red with black: a blue-based, vivid red next to deep black creates the strong contrast you shine in.
avoidColors: Mustard and olive with yellow undertones can make your skin look sallow and tired.
Warm browns and oranges such as camel, terracotta and ochre tend to clash with a cool complexion.
Faded beiges and dusty, grayed-out shades soften the sharp look that suits you.
makeup: Base: Choose a pink-beige or cool ivory with no yellow cast, finished cleanly and evenly rather than overly dewy.
Eyes: Define the lash line with gray, charcoal or cool brown, and add a touch of silver shimmer or plum shading for polish.
Blush: A blue-leaning rose or berry pink, applied lightly high on the cheekbones, brings out a clear flush.
Lips: Fuchsia, cherry red and wine berry work well. A clearly pigmented lip completes the contrast.
fashion: A white shirt with black trousers, or a black jacket over white, is your safest look. Add one vivid accent color to lift it further.
Smooth, subtly lustrous fabrics like silk and satin and sharply tailored shapes suit you. Rough, fuzzy textures can blur your crisp look.
Keep a big light-dark difference between top and bottom. Navy with white or black with pink works better than matching shades of similar brightness.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Blue-black or deep dark brown is reliable. If you dye, consider cool blue-black or a wine-tinted dark shade.
Accessories: Silver, white gold and platinum look best, and clear gemstone colors like sapphire or amethyst make nice accents.
Glasses and small items: Thin, crisp black or silver frames look neat. Matching bags and scarves in black-and-white or vivid cool shades keeps everything tidy.
wintercool.compare: True Winter sits closest to True Summer because both favor blue-based colors, but True Summer is happiest in softened, pastel-like shades while True Winter shines in deeper, sharper ones. Dark Winter also likes dark colors, yet it is built around depth and weight, whereas True Winter is built around cool temperature and crisp contrast. Bright Winter can wear almost neon, high-saturation colors, while True Winter looks most elegant in refined jewel tones. Against a warm type like True Autumn the palettes are nearly opposite, so undertone is the first thing to check.

winterdeep.summary: Deep, cool colors and strong contrast create a mysterious, polished look.
overview: Dark Winter sits at the deepest, darkest end of winter. Like a long night at the turn from autumn into winter, weighty colors make your face look strong and refined.

You do not need to be afraid of low-lightness colors. Navy, deep forest green, wine and rich purple are dark but not muddy, and they actually make your skin look clearer. Adding a touch of white or a vivid accent brings the contrast to life and feels more luxurious.
Pale pastels worn head to toe can overpower you or leave you looking flat. The safest approach is to build outfits from dark shades and use light colors as accents.
features: Skin: Ranges from fair with little yellow to a slightly deeper medium tone, but it generally looks clear and clean.
Hair: Usually deep black or very dark brown, which sharply emphasizes your features.
Eyes: Commonly near-black dark brown, with a clear contrast against the white, giving a deep gaze.
Overall impression: Mysterious, calm and dignified. You look deep even when quiet, and dark clothes tend to make your face look brighter.
bestColors: Black and charcoal: a deep black with a bluish cast and a rich charcoal are your most dependable basics.
Deep navy and ink blue: night-sky blues clarify the skin and add a refined weight.
Rich purple and wine: plum, orchid, dark berry and wine red are the heart of the Dark Winter palette.
Deep green and teal: forest green, emerald and dark teal give calm yet vivid accents.
avoidColors: Cream yellow and pale peach pastels with lots of white can look weak on you.
Light beige, apricot and bright khaki feel warm and soft, and they tend to dull your complexion.
Hazy, watercolor-like low-contrast combinations erase the sharpness that suits you.
makeup: Base: A cool beige without yellow, finished smooth and clean. Avoid foundation that looks chalky or too pale.
Eyes: Deep brown, charcoal, plum and dark wine shadows add depth. You can carry a smoky eye without effort.
Blush: Skip bright coral and choose a calm, blue-leaning rose, berry or dried-rose shade, applied lightly.
Lips: Burgundy, deep red, plum and dark berry are flattering. A well-defined lip balances the whole face.
fashion: All black or black and white works especially well. Even a simple outfit looks finished because the contrast is clear.
Choose fabrics with depth such as velvet, wool and satin, and long, flowing lines. A single purple top or a wine-colored coat can transform the look.
Dress mostly in dark shades but always place one bright accent, like a white shirt or a vivid pink scarf, where you want the eye to land.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Deep black or dark chocolate brown is reliable. Keeping a glossy, rich dark shade usually suits your face better than going light.
Accessories: Silver and white gold, plus deep-colored stones, look best. Amethyst, garnet and sapphire tones make elegant accents.
Glasses and small items: Bold, defined frames in black, deep purple or wine suit you. Leather goods in dark shades keep the look cohesive.
winterdeep.compare: Compared with True Winter and Bright Winter, Dark Winter is centered on the darkest, weightiest colors. True Winter shines through cool temperature and Bright Winter through vivid clarity, while Dark Winter shines through depth. Dark Autumn shares the love of dark colors, so deep wine or green can overlap, but Dark Autumn is comfortable in warm browns and khaki whereas Dark Winter prefers blue-leaning black and navy. Light Spring, with its bright warm pastels, is almost the opposite in color choices.

winterbright.summary: Clear, high-saturation colors and bold contrast give you a sparkling look.
overview: Bright Winter is winter's cool clarity with a touch of spring's fresh energy. In clean, saturated colors your skin looks luminous and your gaze becomes sharper, while cloudy or dull shades take that glow away.

Clarity matters most. Neon-leaning pinks, clear blues and vivid reds that overwhelm other types look polished on you. Pairing them with white or black widens the light-dark gap and keeps the look crisp.
Grayed-out, sunken shades and soft outfits built from similar brightness hide your best qualities. Choose colors that are distinct and combinations that are bold.
features: Skin: Often fair and clear with a blue or neutral pink undertone. Vivid clothing does not swallow your skin.
Hair: Glossy black or very dark brown is common, creating a strong contrast with light skin.
Eyes: Near-black or crisp dark brown, with a clear, sparkling quality.
Overall impression: Lively, defined and striking. You stand out at first glance and tend to look sharp in photos.
bestColors: Pure white and crisp neutrals: optic white, black and a clean silver gray make a tidy base.
Clear blues: vivid sky blue, royal blue and cobalt light up your face.
Bold pinks and magentas: hot pink, fuchsia and bright orchid are signature Bright Winter shades.
Vivid red and deep emerald: a blue-based bright red, a clean green and deep teal make strong accents.
avoidColors: Olive, khaki and mustard with a yellow, dull cast can drain your vitality.
Warm, sunken colors like camel, terracotta and dusty brown make skin look flat.
Grayed muted tones and low-contrast outfits of similar brightness dilute your sharp appeal.
makeup: Base: A clear, translucent cool ivory for a fresh finish. Avoid anything that looks dry or dull.
Eyes: Define with black, navy or vivid purple, and add sparkling silver shimmer to lift your gaze.
Blush: A blue-leaning vivid pink or lively rose, dabbed lightly on the center of the cheeks, brings a clear flush.
Lips: Fuchsia, bright red and vivid pink suit you. A bold, clear pigment finishes the look better than a muted nude.
fashion: A neutral base of white or black plus one vivid color is ideal. Bold pairings such as a black suit with a hot pink top work well.
Glossy materials like leather, patent and satin flatter you, since smooth shine echoes your natural sparkle.
Choose large, clearly lined patterns over tiny prints, and keep the lightness and saturation of top and bottom clearly different.
hairAndAccessories: Hair: Glossy black or deep blue-black is dependable. If you add color, pick a vivid cool shade and keep the shine well maintained.
Accessories: Shiny cool metals such as silver and chrome suit you. Crystals and clear gemstones that reflect light are great choices.
Glasses and small items: Black, transparent or vividly colored frames work well. A single bright bag or pair of shoes can lift the whole outfit.
winterbright.compare: Unlike True Winter and Dark Winter, Bright Winter is centered on high-saturation, clear colors. True Winter shines in refined jewel tones and Dark Winter in deep, dark shades, while Bright Winter can carry near-neon brilliance. Bright Spring shares the love of clear, vivid color, but it is natural in warm coral and yellow-leaning brights, whereas Bright Winter prefers blue-based pinks and blues. Against a type like Soft Autumn, whose palette is gently grayed, the difference in clarity is complete.
